text: 🚨🇲🇽 "There are very right-wing groups in that government that don't like Mexico and that seek a change of government in Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 5, 2026 A reporter noted that Brazil's left had denounced US intervention in its elections and asked if the US could try to intervene in Mexico's 2030 presidential election. "The international right does, yes, it wants to intervene; we have been denouncing it constantly." Of the Trump government, she said it is "not necessarily the President." Her answer: "The only defense is the people, the only one," along with spreading the benefits of the Fourth Transformation and "not zigzagging," as López Obrador used to say.

🇲🇽✊ "Women are not guests of the transformation, we are its protagonists." — Alma Lilia Ruiz Bautista, Tejedora de la Patria, Oaxaca "In a context of external challenges and pressures, women's organization is key to defending the freedom and sovereignty of our homeland." The Tejedoras de la Patria volunteer network now has 197,446 women. The Women's Ministry reported 27 million copies of the women's rights booklet, in 56 Indigenous languages, and 100 Centros LIBRE in all 32 states, with 1.4 million services provided. The goal is one in each of Mexico's nearly 2,500 municipalities. The 079 option 1 hotline has received about 20,000 calls.

🇲🇽🚆 "We are doing our part. We are not sitting with our arms crossed, as it was before, waiting to see who would invest." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 5, 2026 Every major public work of the administration is being tendered now as a multi-year project, so construction runs through 2030 without the usual early-year slowdown. "All the trains are tendered this year," along with highways and water works. The IMF raised its growth forecast for Mexico, and vehicle sales are up more than 8%. The housing chamber told Sheinbaum developers are so busy with the Vivienda para el Bienestar program that "there is even a shortage of labor in some states."

🇲🇽🛢️ Diesel at 27 pesos a liter instead of 35: Mexico keeps subsidizing fuel to stop an inflationary spiral. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 5, 2026 Jet fuel and gasoline prices rose worldwide because of the war in Iran. Mexico stopped collecting the IEPS fuel tax and, some weeks, subsidizes the price outright. Without that support, regular gasoline "should be at about 30 pesos or more today," and diesel above 35. Stations that break the voluntary price agreement receive less support. Subsidizing jet fuel is more complex, Sheinbaum said, which is why international flights have fallen around the world, not only in Mexico. Profeco now counts 8,933 stations selling diesel under 27 pesos.

text:
🇲🇽📊 <u>World Cup Month, Flat Wallets: Mexican Consumption Stalls in July</u>

INEGI data reported by El Economista: Mexican household consumption showed zero growth in July after falling 0.5% in June, despite Mexico co-hosting the World Cup. Year on year it grew 1.1%, the slowest pace since July 2025.

Spending on Mexican-made goods fell 0.2% for the month while spending on imported goods rose 1.4%. So far this year, imported goods are up 8.1%, and domestic goods and services are up just 0.3% each.

🇲🇽✊ <u>Femicides Down 36% a Day, Says Mexico's Women's Secretariat</u>

Mexico's Secretariat for Women reports a historic 36% drop in the daily average of femicides nationwide. It credits community networks, immediate-response hotlines and coordination between agencies.

The Women's Line (079, option 1) has taken about 20,000 calls in just over a year of operation, and femicidal violence was identified in 33% of them. There are now 1,001 Centros LIBRE in every state, covering 40% of municipalities. They have delivered 1,436,869 services and attended 656,344 people with psychological support, legal advice and prevention workshops.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Querétaro's Governor Brought In the US Ambassador. Nobody Told the Foreign Ministry.</u>

PAN governor Mauricio Kuri invited US Ambassador Ronald Johnson to lay the cornerstone of an international police training academy in Querétaro, one focused on organized crime, which falls under federal jurisdiction. Neither the governor nor the ambassador notified Mexico's Foreign Ministry (SRE). Kuri didn't invite the Defense Secretary or the Security Cabinet either.

Sheinbaum says any training agreement between a foreign government and a state must be authorized by the SRE beforehand. Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco will ask both the governor and the US embassy for formal explanations.
banner: QUERÉTARO: US ENVOY IN, SRE LEFT OUT

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>UN Food Chief: Mexico Leads the Fight Against Hunger</u>

Carl Skau, acting executive director of the UN World Food Programme, says Mexico is playing a leadership role against hunger, and that its anti-poverty and nutrition policies hold lessons other countries can use. He pointed to the social programs, the hot and cold school breakfasts, buying food directly from small producers, the rules on what can be sold in schools, and front-of-package warning labels.

Worldwide, acute hunger tripled from 100 million people in 2020 to 300 million in 2025. In Mexico, undernourishment fell from 4.0% in 2004–2006 to 3.1% in 2023–2025.
banner: UN FOOD CHIEF: MEXICO LEADS ON HUNGER
